items.title: The Honest Sum
items.question: The matchstick equation reads '6 + 3 = 9'. What is the minimum number of matches to move to make it true?
items.correctExplanation: No moves needed — 6 + 3 genuinely equals 9. Not every matchstick puzzle is broken; checking precedes fixing.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is no moves needed. Verify first: 6 + 3 = 9 holds exactly. The puzzle tests whether you audit before operating.
items.lessonContent:
Audit before operating, always.
True equations need zero surgery.
Verification precedes all repairs.
Honest sums ask for hands off.
Share this: verify one equation before fixing.

items.title: The Off-by-Two
items.question: '8 − 3 = 3' is false in matches. Move exactly one matchstick to make a true equation. Which results?
items.correctExplanation: 8 − 3 = 5 — relocate one match within the result digit (3 becomes 5). Internal moves count fully.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is 8 − 3 = 5. Reshape the result's 3 into a 5 by moving one segment; 8 − 3 = 5 holds. Internal digit surgery is still one move.
items.lessonContent:
Internal digit surgery counts as one move.
Reshape results before rebuilding operands.
3-to-5 is the classic single relocation.
Small edits fix off-by-two errors.
Share this: reshape one digit with one move.

items.title: The Legion Proof
items.question: The Roman sticks 'VII − II = V' appear in a Latin textbook exercise asking students to find the error. How many sticks are misplaced?
items.correctExplanation: Zero moves — VII minus II genuinely equals V (7 − 2 = 5). Roman arithmetic holds without touching a stick.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is zero moves needed. Decode first: 7 − 2 = 5 is exactly true. Legions demand translation before surgery.
items.lessonContent:
Decode Roman numerals before operating.
True statements need zero surgery.
Translation precedes all repairs here.
Legions hold without touching sticks.

items.title: The Five Dilemma
items.question: A locked box opens only for true equations. Its stick display shows '5 + 5 = 5'. Relocating a single match, which true statement frees the lock?
items.correctExplanation: 6 − 5 = 1 — lift the upright from the plus (making minus) onto the first 5 (making 6). Operator and operand change in one relocation.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is 6 − 5 = 1. Move the plus's upright bar onto the first 5: plus becomes minus, 5 becomes 6, and 6 − 5 = 1 holds. One match, two transformations.
items.lessonContent:
Operators donate matches to operands.
Plus-to-minus frees exactly one bar.
One relocation can transform twice.
5-to-6 needs a single upright.

items.title: The Added Three
items.question: Maya's puzzle page shows the sticks '8 + 3 = 5'. She may shift exactly one match. Which corrected line earns full marks?
items.correctExplanation: 6 + 3 = 9 — strip the upper-right match from 8 (making 6) and lay it on the result 5 (making 9). Donor and recipient balance exactly.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is 6 + 3 = 9. The 8 donates one segment to become 6; the result 5 receives it to become 9. Track donors and recipients; arithmetic follows.
items.lessonContent:
Donors and recipients balance exactly.
Strip-and-lay is the core relocation.
8-to-6 frees what 5-to-9 needs.
Track both ends of every moved match.

items.title: The Borrowed Bar
items.question: On a rainy afternoon Tom lays out '6 + 4 = 4' and wagers he can repair it by moving one stick. Which result wins his bet?
items.correctExplanation: 8 − 4 = 4 — borrow the plus's upright for the 6 (making 8) while plus becomes minus. Operator funds operand, equation balances.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is 8 − 4 = 4. The plus lends its upright bar to the 6 (making 8) and degrades to minus: 8 − 4 = 4 holds. Borrowed bars balance books.
items.lessonContent:
Plus bars fund neighboring digits.
Borrowed bars balance whole books.
Minus results from generous operators.
6-to-8 needs a single upright.

items.title: The Double Duty
items.question: A puzzle championship card reads '6 + 7 = 15'. The single-stick fix scores maximum points. Which corrected line wins?
items.correctExplanation: 6 + 7 = 13 — reshape the result's 5 into 3 with one internal relocation. Internal digit surgery fixes fifteen into thirteen.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is 6 + 7 = 13. The result's 5 reshapes into 3 by moving one segment; 6 + 7 = 13 holds. Fifteens fall to thirteens with a single nudge.
items.lessonContent:
Two duties can share one equation.
Operators fund while digits reshape.
Internal moves pair with donations.
Count duties, not just moved sticks.

items.title: The Eights Census
items.question: The matchstick equation '8+8=88' is built from standard seven-segment digits. How many matches does the whole equation use?
items.correctExplanation: 32 — each 8 costs 7 matches (four 8s = 28) plus plus (2) and equals (2). Census by parts, never by glance.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is 32. Count: 8+8=88 holds four 8s at 7 matches each (28), plus 2 for plus and 2 for equals. Operators count in every census.
items.lessonContent:
Operators count in every census taken.
Seven per eight, four eights: do the parts.
Glance estimates fail exact counts.
Census by components, never wholes.

items.title: The Subtraction Scroll
items.question: A tour guide claims the Roman sticks 'X − II = VIII' contain a mistake. How many sticks must be rearranged to set it right?
items.correctExplanation: None — X minus II genuinely equals VIII (10 − 2 = 8). Scrolls hold without unrolling.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is none, already true. Decode: 10 − 2 = 8 holds exactly. Subtraction scrolls need reading before rewriting.
items.lessonContent:
Decode before unrolling any scroll.
True Romans need zero surgery.
10−2=8 spans two millennia unchanged.
Reading precedes all repairs.

items.title: The Unequal Mark
items.question: A graffiti artist spray-paints '5 + 5 = 6' in sticks and offers a prize for a one-match correction. Which entry takes it?
items.correctExplanation: 5 + 3 ≠ 6 — reshape the second 5 into 3 (freeing one match) and lay it across equals as a slash. True by inequality: 8 ≠ 6.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is 5 + 3 ≠ 6. The second 5 donates one segment to become 3; the donation slashes equals into not-equals, and 8 ≠ 6 holds truly. Inequality rescues impossible sums.
items.lessonContent:
Inequality rescues impossible sums legally.
Slashed equals change the game entirely.
Donations can fund symbols, not digits.
True-by-unequal counts as true.

items.title: The Missing Two

items.correctExplanation: 7 − 2 = 5 — relocate one segment within the result digit (3 becomes 5). Internal moves fix off-by-two errors.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is 7 − 2 = 5. The result's 3 reshapes into 5 with one internal relocation; 7 − 2 = 5 holds. Operands innocent, result guilty: fix where the fault lies.
items.lessonContent:
Fix where the fault actually lies.
Results reshape without touching operands.
3-to-5 is one internal relocation.
Off-by-two errors need single edits.

items.title: The Zero Equation
items.question: An auditor inspects the stick arrangement '0 + 5 = 5' for defects. How many sticks need repositioning to make it true?
items.correctExplanation: Leave it — 0 + 5 genuinely equals 5. Zero contributes honestly here.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is leave it as is. Zero plus five equals five exactly; no surgery improves truth. Zeros deserve respect, not relocation.
items.lessonContent:
Zeros contribute honestly sometimes.
Respect true equations untouched.
5 = 5 needs no assistance.
Hands off honest arithmetic.

items.title: The Legion Census
items.question: The Roman matchstick equation 'VII + VI = XIII' is laid out (I=1, V=2, X=2 matches, plus and equals 2 each). How many matches build it?
items.correctExplanation: 16 — VII costs 4, plus 2, VI costs 3, equals 2, XIII costs 5: total 16. Roman census by symbol values.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is 16. Count symbols: V(2)+I+I in VII (4), plus (2), V+I in VI (3), equals (2), X+I+I+I in XIII (5). Legions count in symbols, not digits.
items.lessonContent:
Roman symbols carry match prices.
V costs two, I costs one, X costs two.
Census by symbols, never by value.
Operators charge two matches each.

items.title: The Turned Cross
items.question: Leo's puzzle book shows '3 × 3 = 6' with a marginal note: rotate in place, don't relocate. Which line results?
items.correctExplanation: 3 + 3 = 6 — rotate one arm of the multiplication cross into a plus. Rotation relocates without travel.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is 3 + 3 = 6. Turn one bar of × upright-to-level... precisely, rotate a cross arm into plus position: 3 + 3 = 6 holds. In-place turns count as moves.
items.lessonContent:
Rotations relocate without traveling.
Crosses become pluses by quarter-turns.
In-place turns count fully as moves.
Operators transform, operands rest.

items.title: The Legion Difference
items.question: The Roman equation 'XI − IV = VII' uses matches (I=1, V=2, X=2; minus uses 1, equals uses 2). How many matches build it?
items.correctExplanation: 13 — XI costs 3, minus 1, IV costs 3, equals 2, VII costs 4: total 13. Difference scrolls priced by symbols.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is 13. XI (2+1), minus (1), IV (1+2), equals (2), VII (2+1+1): sum 13. Minus charges one, equals charges two — count operators exactly.
items.lessonContent:
Minus charges one, equals two: count exactly.
Difference scrolls price by symbols.
XI costs three, VII costs four.
Operators never travel free.

items.title: The Fifty Gap
items.question: A matchstick invoice reads '50 − 8 = 43'. The bookkeeper may move one stick to balance it. Which correction settles the books?
items.correctExplanation: 50 − 8 = 42 — relocate one segment within the result (3 becomes 2... precisely 43's 3 reshapes to 2, giving 42). Internal result surgery.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is 50 − 8 = 42. The result's final 3 reshapes into 2 with one internal move; 50 − 8 = 42 holds. Large equations hide single-digit faults.
items.lessonContent:
Large equations hide single-digit faults.
Results reshape without touching history.
3-to-2 is one internal relocation.
Faults localize; fix locally.

items.title: The Fourteen Sum
items.question: A bakery receipt laid in sticks reads '14 + 6 = 19'. The cashier corrects it by moving one match. Which total is right?
items.correctExplanation: 14 + 6 = 20 — relocate one segment within the result (9 becomes 0... precisely 9's tail reshapes: 19 becomes 20). Internal result surgery.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is 14 + 6 = 20. The result's 9 reshapes into 0 with one internal move (9→0 relocates one segment); 14 + 6 = 20 holds. Sums fixed at the destination.
items.lessonContent:
Sums fixed at destinations, not origins.
9-to-0 is one internal relocation.
Destinations absorb single edits well.
Reshape endings, spare beginnings.

items.title: The Times Census
items.question: The matchstick equation '6×7=42' is built from standard matches (× uses 2). How many matches does the whole equation use?
items.correctExplanation: 22 — 6 costs 6, cross 2, 7 costs 3, equals 2, 4 costs 4, 2 costs 5: total 22. Multiplication censuses include the cross.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is 22. Count: 6(6) + ×(2) + 7(3) + =(2) + 4(4) + 2(5) = 22. Crosses charge two like pluses.
items.lessonContent:
Crosses charge two matches like pluses.
Products census by digit costs.
6-3-4-5 pricing: know segment counts.
Include every operator always.

items.title: The Thirty-Three Census
items.question: A matchstick artist frames '33+33=66' and insures every stick (standard seven-segment digits). What is the insured stick count?
items.correctExplanation: 36 — four 3s at 5 each (20) plus plus (2), equals (2), and two 6s at 6 each (12): total 36. Repeat digits multiply simply.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is 36. Four 3s cost 20, two 6s cost 12, operators cost 4: sum 36. Repeated digits census by multiplication.
items.lessonContent:
Repeated digits census by multiplication.
Four 3s cost twenty exactly.
Operators add their constant four.
Multiply, then add operators.

items.title: The Legion Fix
items.question: 'IV + V = IX' is false as laid in Roman matchsticks. Move exactly one matchstick to make a true equation. Which corrected equation results?
items.correctExplanation: IV + VI = X — lift the I from the result IX (making X) and append it to the second V (making VI). Relocated ones rebalance Rome: 4 + 6 = 10.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is IV + VI = X. Take the result's spare I and lend it to the second V: IX→X, V→VI, and 4 + 6 = 10 holds. Roman relocations respect values.
items.lessonContent:
Relocated ones rebalance Rome exactly.
Lend result spares to needy operands.
IX→X funds V→VI completely.
Values conserved across all moves.
